t: Before you is the Earl Haig Memorial, a bronze equestrian statue on Whitehall. It shows Douglas Haig, who commanded the British Expeditionary Force on the Western Front from late 1915 until the end of the First World War. The sculptor was Alfred Frank Hardiman, and Parliament commissioned it in 1928. It took eight years to make and stirred real controversy. Critics attacked the Field Marshal's riding position, his uniform, and the horse's anatomy and stance. The plinth names him Commander-in-Chief of the British Armies in France, 1915 to 1918.
